'''Immanuel Bloch''' (born 16 November 1972, [[Fulda]]) is a German  [[experimental physicist]]. His research is focused on the investigation of quantum [[Many-body problem|many-body]] systems using ultracold atomic and molecular quantum gases. Bloch is known for his work on atoms in artificial crystals of light, [[optical lattice]]s, especially the first realization of a quantum [[phase transition]] from a weakly interacting [[superfluid]] to a strongly interacting [[Mott Insulator|Mott insulating state of matter]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Immanuel Bloch {{!}} Max-Planck-Institute for Quantum Optics |url=https://www.mpq.mpg.de/person/34641/4743113 |access-date=2023-01-12 |website=www.mpq.mpg.de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Immanuel Bloch |url=https://hector-fellow-academy.de/en/research/hector-fellows/immanuel-bloch/ |access-date=2023-01-12 |website=Hector Fellow Academy |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bloch, Immanuel |url=https://www.mpg.de/465966/quantum-optics-bloch |access-date=2023-01-26 |website=www.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Bloch studied physics at the University of Bonn in 1995, followed by a one-year research visit to [[Stanford University]].<ref name="Max-Planck-Gesellschaft 2021">{{cite web | title=Bloch, Immanuel | website=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft | date=21 October 2021 | url=https://www.mpg.de/465966/quantenoptik_wissM184 | access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref> He obtained his PhD in 2000 working under [[Theodor W. Hänsch]] at [[LMU Munich]].<ref name="Max-Planck-Gesellschaft 2021" /> The thesis title was ''Atomlaser und Phasenkohärenz atomarer Bose-Einstein-Kondensate''.<ref>[https://edoc.ub.uni-muenchen.de/208/1/Bloch_Immanuel.pdf thesis]</ref> As a junior group leader, he continued in Munich and started his work on ultracold quantum gases in optical lattices. In 2003, he moved to a full professor position in experimental physics at the [[University of Mainz]], where he stayed until 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Bloch_Immanuel_D.pdf|title=CV|accessdate=16 December 2021}}</ref>

In 2008 he was appointed scientific director of the newly founded division on ''Quantum Many-Body Systems'' at the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]] in Garching.<ref name="Quantum Optics Group 2021">{{cite web | title=Bloch, Immanuel Prof. Dr. | website=Quantum Optics Group | date=18 November 2021 | url=https://www.quantum-munich.de/104554/bloch-immanuel-prof-dr | access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref> Since 2012 he has been vice-dean at the department of physics of LMU Munich<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physik.lmu.de/de/index.html|title=Willkommen an der Fakultät für Physik|website=www.physik.lmu.de|accessdate=16 December 2021}}</ref> and managing director of the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]] since 2012.

==Research==
Bloch's work focuses on the investigation of quantum many-body system using [[Ultracold atom|ultracold atoms]]<ref name="Bloch Dalibard Zwerger pp. 885–964">{{cite journal | last1=Bloch | first1=Immanuel | last2=Dalibard | first2=Jean | last3=Zwerger | first3=Wilhelm | title=Many-body physics with ultracold gases | journal=Reviews of Modern Physics | volume=80 | issue=3 | date=18 July 2008 | issn=0034-6861 | doi=10.1103/revmodphys.80.885 | pages=885–964| arxiv=0704.3011 | bibcode=2008RvMP...80..885B | s2cid=119618473 }}</ref> stored in [[optical lattice]] potentials. Among other things, he is known for the realization of a [[quantum phase transition]] from a [[superfluid]] to a [[Mott insulator]],<ref name="Greiner Mandel Esslinger Hänsch 2002 pp. 39–44">{{cite journal | last1=Greiner | first1=Markus | last2=Mandel | first2=Olaf | last3=Esslinger | first3=Tilman | last4=Hänsch | first4=Theodor W. | last5=Bloch | first5=Immanuel | title=Quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator in a gas of ultracold atoms | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=415 | issue=6867 | year=2002 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/415039a | pages=39–44| pmid=11780110 | bibcode=2002Natur.415...39G | s2cid=4411344 | arxiv=2506.21303 }}</ref> in which ultracold atoms were brought into the regime of strong correlations for the first time, thereby allowing one to mimic the behaviour [[strongly correlated material]]s. The experimental ideas were based on a theoretical proposal by [[Peter Zoller]] and [[Ignacio Cirac]]. His other works includes the observation of a [[Tonks–Girardeau gas]]<ref name="Paredes Widera Murg Mandel 2004 pp. 277–281">{{cite journal | last1=Paredes | first1=Belén | last2=Widera | first2=Artur | last3=Murg | first3=Valentin | last4=Mandel | first4=Olaf | last5=Fölling | first5=Simon | last6=Cirac | first6=Ignacio | last7=Shlyapnikov | first7=Gora V. | last8=Hänsch | first8=Theodor W. | last9=Bloch | first9=Immanuel | title=Tonks–Girardeau gas of ultracold atoms in an optical lattice | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=429 | issue=6989 | year=2004 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/nature02530 | pages=277–281| pmid=15152247 | bibcode=2004Natur.429..277P | s2cid=4423003 }}</ref> of strongly interacting bosons in one dimensions, the detection of collapses and revivals<ref name="Greiner Mandel Hänsch Bloch 2002 pp. 51–54">{{cite journal | last1=Greiner | first1=Markus | last2=Mandel | first2=Olaf | last3=Hänsch | first3=Theodor W. | last4=Bloch | first4=Immanuel | title=Collapse and revival of the matter wave field of a Bose–Einstein condensate | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=419 | issue=6902 | year=2002 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/nature00968 | pages=51–54| pmid=12214228 | arxiv=cond-mat/0207196 | bibcode=2002Natur.419...51G | s2cid=4392894 }}</ref> of the wavefunction of a [[Bose–Einstein condensate]] because of interactions, and the use of quantum noise correlations to observe [[Hanbury Brown and Twiss effect|Hanbury Brown and Twiss]] bunching<ref>S. Fölling, F. Gerbier, A. Widera, O. Mandel, T. Gericke & I. Bloch, Spatial quantum noise interferometry in expanding ultracold atom clouds, [https://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v434/n7032/abs/nature03500.html Nature 434, 481 (2005)]</ref> and antibunching<ref name="Rom Best van Oosten Schneider 2006 pp. 733–736">{{cite journal | last1=Rom | first1=T. | last2=Best | first2=Th. | last3=van Oosten | first3=D. | last4=Schneider | first4=U. | last5=Fölling | first5=S. | last6=Paredes | first6=B. | last7=Bloch | first7=I. | title=Free fermion antibunching in a degenerate atomic Fermi gas released from an optical lattice | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=444 | issue=7120 | year=2006 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/nature05319 | pages=733–736| pmid=17151662 | arxiv=cond-mat/0611561 | bibcode=2006Natur.444..733R | s2cid=4341076 }}</ref> for bosonic and fermionic atoms (simultaneously with the group of  [[Alain Aspect]]). More recently, his research team was able to realize single-atom resolved imaging<ref name="Sherson Weitenberg Endres Cheneau pp. 68–72">{{cite journal | last1=Sherson | first1=Jacob F. | last2=Weitenberg | first2=Christof | last3=Endres | first3=Manuel | last4=Cheneau | first4=Marc | last5=Bloch | first5=Immanuel | last6=Kuhr | first6=Stefan | title=Single-atom-resolved fluorescence imaging of an atomic Mott insulator | journal=Nature | volume=467 | issue=7311 | date=18 August 2010 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/nature09378 | pages=68–72| pmid=20720540 | arxiv=1006.3799 | bibcode=2010Natur.467...68S | s2cid=4385923 }}</ref> and addressing<ref name="Weitenberg Endres Sherson Cheneau 2011 pp. 319–324">{{cite journal | last1=Weitenberg | first1=Christof | last2=Endres | first2=Manuel | last3=Sherson | first3=Jacob F. | last4=Cheneau | first4=Marc | last5=Schauß | first5=Peter | last6=Fukuhara | first6=Takeshi | last7=Bloch | first7=Immanuel | last8=Kuhr | first8=Stefan | title=Single-spin addressing in an atomic Mott insulator | journal=Nature | volume=471 | issue=7338 | year=2011 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/nature09827 | pages=319–324| pmid=21412333 | arxiv=1101.2076 | bibcode=2011Natur.471..319W | s2cid=4352129 }}</ref> of ultracold atoms held in an optical lattice. Much of his related work was carried out in the group of [[Markus Greiner]].

==Awards==
In 2005 he was presented with the International Commission of Optics Prize. In 2011, he received the EPS Prize for Fundamental Aspects of Quantum Electronics and Optics<ref name="EPS Quantum Electronics and Optics Division (QEOD) – EPS Quantum Electronics and Optics Division (QEOD) 2021">{{cite web | title=EPS-QEOD Quantum Electronics and Optics Prize – EPS Quantum Electronics and Optics Division (QEOD) | website=EPS Quantum Electronics and Optics Division (QEOD) – EPS Quantum Electronics and Optics Division (QEOD) | date=19 November 2021 | url=https://qeod.epsdivisions.org/eps-qeod-quantum-electronics-and-optics-prize/ | access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref> of the [[European Physical Society]].

In 2013, Bloch was awarded the [[Körber European Science Prize]] and the International Senior BEC Award. For the year 2015 he received the [[Harvey Prize]] from Israel's Technion Institute.<ref>[https://harveypz.net.technion.ac.il/harvey-prize-laureates/ Harvey Prize Laureates]</ref> In 2024 he received the [[Stern–Gerlach Medal]] of the German Physical Society.<ref>[https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise/stern-gerlach-medaille/preistraeger Stern–Gerlach Medal 2024]</ref> In 2026 he was awarded the [[Wolf Prize in Physics]].<ref>[https://wolffund.org.il/immanuel-f-bloch/ Wolf Prize 2026]</ref>

He is a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] and an external member of the [[Canadian Institute for Advanced Research]].
